_comment: TEMPLATE. Copy to tools/board_registry.json, which is gitignored, and
let `python tools/identify_boards.py --learn` fill it in from the
boards on YOUR desk.
WHY THIS FILE IS A TEMPLATE AND THE REAL ONE IS NEVER COMMITTED.
A board's MAC is burned into eFuse: it cannot be changed, ever. So
publishing one publishes a permanent identifier for a specific piece
of hardware in somebody's home -- and publishing it in THIS file
publishes it next to the exact firmware that board runs, which is
strictly worse than either fact alone. The real registry was tracked
for three commits and reached two releases before this was caught;
see CLAUDE.md, 'No identifiers in this repository'.
The MACs below are placeholders and match no real device. The map is
still keyed by MAC because that is the only identifier that survives
a replug, a reflash and an empty flash chip -- a COM number is
assigned in plug order and is stale by the next reboot.
`how` records what an identification RESTS on. 'boot banner' and
'confirmed on the panel by the owner' are different levels of
confidence and this file must not hide which one it has: the banner
is compiled in, so it reports the firmware on the chip rather than
the panel underneath it.

aa:bb:cc:00:00:01.note: Placeholder. Replace with your own board via --learn.
aa:bb:cc:00:00:01.how: example entry, not a real device

aa:bb:cc:00:00:02.note: Placeholder. The only ESP32-S3 in the set, so chip type alone identifies it.
